source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI), Adi Parva, adhyaya 2 (Samantapanchaka), vv. 1–9

voice.note: speaker → script/cast.json (voice, speed, pitch). Per line: speed (× the speaker's), pre/post (ms of silence before/after the voice, used by the timeline), say (what is spoken, if not `text`): '…' and '—' pause, [p:400] pauses 400 ms, {s:0.8} speaks what follows at 0.8× until the next {s:…} ({s} resets).

lines.speaker: elder_sage
lines.text: Tell us, son of the Suta… where was that great war fought?
lines.note: beats[0] = 'where': the elder leans in and his hand opens

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: In a sacred land… called Samantapanchaka.
lines.note: beats = 'land' (the fire flares), the name (the map of the land settles; the name is written in gold)

lines.text: Long before, the warrior-sage Parashurama, axe in hand…
lines.note: beats = the name (lightning reveals him), 'axe' (the axe reaches the top of its raise; thunder)

lines.text: …struck down the warrior kings. Twenty-one times.
lines.note: ticks = 21 hits from 'struck' to 'Twenty-one', accelerating: a crown falls and a tally mark is cut on each; the 21st lands on 'Twenty-one' with XXI (beats[0])

lines.text: With their blood, he filled five great lakes.
lines.note: beats = 'filled' (the first lake fills), 'five' (all five are filling), 'lakes' (the mandala glows)

lines.text: His ancestors appeared, and asked him to stop. He did — and the land became holy.
lines.say: His ancestors appeared, and asked him to stop. [p:280] He did — {s:0.86}and the land became holy.
lines.note: beats = 'appeared' (the Pitrs are down), 'stop' (palms out), 'did' (the axe is lowered), 'holy' (the water is clear, lotuses open)

lines.text: Ages later, on that same ground… two great armies would meet.
lines.note: beats = 'two' (the standards rise on both horizons), 'meet' (a conch)

lines.text: Episode two. The field of five lakes.
lines.say: Episode two. [p:200] The field of five lakes.
lines.note: spoken over the end card, which shows strings.episodeLabel / episodeTitle instead of a caption
